title: Limits of the level-independent fall: level superpositions, records, the operator under the factor

key_results.statement: For a level-superposed start the place weights are the exact mixture $p_x=\sum_k\lvert\alpha_k\rvert^2p^{(k)}_x$ and $\bar x_{\rm lab}=\sum_k\lvert\alpha_k\rvert^2\bar x_k$, exact in the gradients and in $\kappa$; it rests on the conservation of the level and the orthonormality of the $\lvert f_k\rangle$.

The drift acceleration of the mean position label is $\sum_k\lvert\alpha_k\rvert^2a_{k,\sigma}(p_0)$ (first order in the gradients, long chain, long window, then sharp label); it is the same for all $\alpha$ iff $a_{k,\sigma}(p_0)$ is level-independent, which at rest is the condition (4.19) unchanged.

For a start at rest the variance over the levels of the first-order displacements is $\tfrac14\lambda^4\operatorname{Var}_\alpha(\langle a_{\cdot,\sigma}\rangle_g)+E$ with $\lvert E\rvert\le r\lambda^3\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_\alpha}+r^2\lambda^2$, and $\operatorname{Var}_\alpha(a_{\cdot,\sigma}(0))$ in the sharp-label limit taken last.

With $\lvert\alpha_k\rvert^2=1/N$ the $\lambda^4$ part is $0$ for the variants (a), (c), $\tfrac14\lambda^4\tau^4g^2m^2\mathcal V_N$ for (b1), (b2) and $\tfrac14\lambda^4\tau^4g^2c_{\rm f}^2\mathcal V_N$ for (f), with $\mathcal V_N$ the variance of $1/M_k$ over the levels.

At zero gradients the level components move with $\sigma\langle\omega_k'\rangle_g\to\sigma\omega_k'(p_0)$; in the class $\mathcal C$ no two levels have equal velocities for $\sin2p_0\neq0$, and in $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ equality at one $p_0$ requires $\tau_k^4/(M_k^2+\tau_k^2\sin^2p_0)$ to coincide.

Exactly in the gradients, the mean label of a normalized level component obeys $\mathrm d\bar p_k/\mathrm d\lambda=-\int\frac{\mathrm dp}{2\pi}c^\dagger B_kc+(c^\dagger B_kc)(p_0+\pi)$, the last term being the weight crossing the cut of the arc.

To first order in the gradients the label rate of a branch start is $\langle\pi_{k,\sigma}\rangle_g$ up to the cut term, with $\pi_{k,\sigma}(0)=\mathcal F_k-\sigma G_k$ at rest; it is level-independent iff $\mathcal F_k-\sigma G_k$ is, and together with a nonzero level-independent fall iff also $\tau_k^2/M_k$ is level-independent, which is impossible in the class $\mathcal C$.

The clock-label statistics is $P(a;\lambda)=\frac1N\sum_{k,k'}\alpha_{k'}^*\alpha_k\Gamma_{kk'}(\lambda)e^{2\pi i(k-k')a/N}$, with the coherences of the effective body contract at leading order in $\kappa$.

At zero gradients $\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}=e^{-i(V_k-V_{k'})\lambda}\langle\cos\tfrac{\theta_k-\theta_{k'}}2e^{-i\sigma(\omega_k-\omega_{k'})\lambda}\rangle_g$, and for even $g$ the coherence $\Gamma_{kk'}$ is exactly even in the gradients, so $\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert$ first deviates at second order.

Order estimate for a Gaussian even start at rest: $1-\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert/\lvert\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}\rvert\simeq\tfrac12\delta x^2(\pi_k-\pi_{k'})^2\lambda^2+\tfrac{\lambda^4}{32\delta x^2}\bigl(\tfrac{\tau_{k'}^2}{M_{k'}}\pi_k-\tfrac{\tau_k^2}{M_k}\pi_{k'}\bigr)^2$ with $\pi_k=\mathcal F_k-\sigma G_k$; it does not vanish for a nonzero level-independent fall unless $\tau_k^2/M_k$ is level-independent.

At first order jointly in $G_k$, $\mathcal F_k$, $g_{\zeta,k}$ and $\kappa(\xi-\langle X\rangle)$ the first-order velocity of a branch start, and with it (4.7), (4.16), (4.19), does not change when $X$ is not sharp, because the velocity is linear and $\xi-\langle X\rangle$ has zero mean.

At zero gradients the coefficient of $\varepsilon^2$ in the velocity at the label $p$ is $v_2=\sigma[\tfrac12\lambda^2\omega'''-\tfrac{\theta'\theta''}{4\omega}(1-\cos2\omega\lambda)-\tfrac{\lambda}{2\omega}\theta'(\omega\theta')'\sin2\omega\lambda-\tfrac12\lambda^2\theta'^2\omega'\cos2\omega\lambda]$, exact for all $\lambda$.

The mean velocity is $\sigma\langle\omega_k'\rangle_g+\kappa^2\sigma_X^2[\tfrac12\lambda^2\sigma\langle\omega_k'''\rangle_g+R_2]+\kappa^3\mu_3[-\tfrac16\lambda^3\sigma\langle\omega_k''''\rangle_g+R_3]+O(\kappa^4)$ at fixed $\lambda$, start and chain, with an exact bound $R_2=O(\lambda)$ depending on $X_g$ and the order estimate $R_3=O(\lambda^{5/2})$.

For a sharp label the second-order records change the acceleration by $\delta a^{(2)}_{k,\sigma}=-\kappa^2\sigma_X^2\lambda v(4+3\omega_k''(p_0)/\omega_k(p_0))=-\kappa^2\sigma_X^2\lambda(4+3\tau_k^2/M_k^2)v+O(v^3)$: zero at rest, first order in $v$, branch-independent at given $v$, level-independent iff $\tau_k/M_k$ is.

The third-order term is $\delta a^{(3)}_{k,\sigma}=-\tfrac12\kappa^3\mu_3\lambda^2\sigma\omega_k''''(p_0)$, at rest $\tfrac\sigma2\kappa^3\mu_3\lambda^2\tfrac{\tau_k^2}{M_k}(4+\tfrac{3\tau_k^2}{M_k^2})$: nonzero only for a skewed $X$, odd in the branch and level-dependent in the class $\mathcal C$.

In the background of (17.15) the record terms are $[-\lambda(4d_0^2+3v_{\max,k}^2/M_k^2)u+\tfrac{\sigma\gamma_X}2\lambda^2\tfrac{v_{\max,k}^2}{M_k}(4d_0^2+3v_{\max,k}^2/M_k^2)]\hat e$ with $u=d_0v$, $\gamma_X=\mu_3/\sigma_X^3$.

The record terms are smaller than the drift acceleration at rest iff the ratios $\varrho_2$ and $\varrho_3$ are below one; a level-independent fall to the relative accuracy $\delta_{\rm acc}$ requires $\varrho_2,\varrho_3\le\delta_{\rm acc}$ for all levels on the whole range of $\lambda$ and $v$, a condition not uniform in $\lambda$ or in the gradients.
For the on-site block $(1+gx)[M_k\sigma_3+u_k]-\mathcal F_Ux$ the fall from rest is $a_{k,\pm}(0)=-g\tau_k^2\pm\tfrac{\tau_k^2}{M_k}(\mathcal F_U-gu_k)$, for arbitrary hopping factors.

The fall from rest is level-independent in the upper (lower) branch iff $\tau_k^2[\pm(\mathcal F_U-gu_k)/M_k-g]$ is level-independent, and in both branches with one value $a$ iff $gu_k=\mathcal F_U$ and $g\tau_k^2=-a$ for all $k$.

Adding $c\,\mathbb 1$ to the effective body contract acts as $(u_k,\mathcal F_U)\mapsto(u_k+c,\mathcal F_U+gc)$; well defined are $g$, $M_k$, $u_k-u_{k'}$ and $\mathcal F_U-gu_k$, while $u_k$, the statement $u_k=0$ for all $k$ and the statement $u_k\propto M_k$ are not.

Table of the orders in the gradients, $v$, $M_k/\tau_k$, $\kappa$ and $\lambda$ at which the lattice, the drift velocity, a level superposition, the records, the operator under the factor and a plain gradient change the level-independent fall and the relation (4.24).

open_issues: The coefficients of (7.10) are an order estimate under the conditions E1–E3 (Gaussian even start, within-branch transport, equal spreading); a bound for general g and the first-order term for starts that are not even are not derived.

R_3 = O(λ^(5/2)) in (7.14) and the window suppression O(1/(M_k Λ)) of the oscillating terms for a sharp label are order estimates; only R_2 has an exact bound, and it is not uniform in the sharp-label limit.
The estimate of the ratio ϱ_2 for a fall from rest mixes κ² with a gradient (third order, out of scope) and is not derived.
(7.17) uses the maximal speed τ_k d_0 for level-dependent τ_k, while the quoted bound (5.11) of 04-ilang-time/05-moving-clock is stated for one τ.

The effect of an operator under the factor on the relation (4.24) outside the class C (for example u_k = u_* + w M_k with w ≠ 0) needs the clock rate of that body, which is not among the quoted inputs.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions: (7.15), (7.16) have the unit of an acceleration in position labels per λ², and (7.10), (7.3), ϱ_2, ϱ_3 are dimensionless.
One level only and a sharp X: (7.1)–(7.3) reduce to the single-level start with a uniform clock-label statistics 1/N, and (7.11), (7.14)–(7.17) reduce to (4.5).
Short-λ expansion of (7.13) agrees with the double commutator ½λ²ε²⟨C_0'''⟩, and the label rate (7.7) reproduces (4.16) through a = σ ω''(0) dp/dλ.
